title: Princess Airhead
text:
First of all, previous reviewer is right; Princess Celestia is a white unicorn. My daughter saw her in the book and fell in love with her. Why is she pink? Even on the box the pink one comes in she is white! Secondly she says the most inane nonsense you can imagine, "my hair is sooo beautiful", "my wings are sooo beautiful". Not really what I want my 4 year old hearing. (although I guess it beats the barbie I got as a child that told me "math is hard")

To be honest, I noticed the button on her hip while at the store. I pressed it and it made a magic wand style brrriiiingg noise and her wings flashed. Had I the presence of mind to press it again, I would have known that she talks. I brought it home and gave it to my daughter who immediately pressed the button a 2nd time and I immediately regretted my decision.

That being said, she loves the stupid thing. She keeps it on a high shelf so her brother (1yr) can't get it. Of course sometimes he does and he loves it too. She doesn't play with it like other dolls and ponies- there is little interaction with other characters, no dialogue, limited pretend situations. She takes this one down and looks at it, presses the button, maybe brushes the hair and thats it. But she is enamored with it. So much so that she accepted, without question, whatever nonsense I told her about why she is pink and not white.

title: DJI Phantom 3 Advanced...Awesome Drone!! Love this thing!
text: Purchased this after reviewing many drones and researching for almost 1 year.  I absolutely love this thing!  My very first drone.  If you like photography, or just the fun of flying a drone, this is for you.  It's very easy to fly.  I use my ipad mini as the console.  The batteries each last approx 25 minutes.  Flight speed up to 35 mph.  On a very clear day, with no obstructions, I have been able to fly this out approx 3,000 feet without concern; then it gets a little "fuzzy" and I start to get the "weak signal" message.  I have flown at night.  I did crash it once into a tree (my fault, I wasn't paying attention).  I had it repaired at Drone Nerds in FL.  Excellent service!  My most recent scare.....It was out approx 2,500 feet and my iPad overheated and went blank.  I thought it was toast.....never to be seen again.  It came back to me, as advertised!  Awesome!!  Two lessons learned....be sure the home-point is updated at every takeoff (otherwise it would have been lost) & be careful in hot weather (my ipad completely shutdown unexpectedly).  The hardest part....upon initial purchase, getting the software updated on the Drone and the Remote control.  Take a deep breath...."patience" is the key word.  Once you figure it out the first time, it's easy from there.

title: Great Tool for Imaginative Fun but Do your Research
text:
Made for a very interesting and unique gift that requires a little bit of work, creativity, and imagination that I think is needed these days. My niece wanted this and I had no idea what it was so I researched it a little and was surprised that she knew what this was and wanted it. While there are a lot of ways to play with this at its base it is fairly simple and easy to learn and use. I appreciate that it combines gaming and electronics with a little bit of learning, creativity, imagination and inventiveness.

I gave it only 4 stars because I don't think this is for everyone. If you're planning to buy this for a present, you should really see if this is the kind of thing that person/child wants. If you think someone might like it as a gift they might also need someone to show them the kind of fun they can enjoy with this. It is an interesting concept and the possibilities are near limitless but I think anyone that hasn't researched the Makey Makey at all and are considering it for a gift, to really read into what it is and what it can be.

The price is a little steep in my opinion at about $50. I think $35-$40 would have been a sweet spot but it is well made and designed and I have no issue spending a little more to support innovative ideas. I can happily recommend this.

title: Great for a toddler's hands. A 7-inch Buzz Lightyear is perfect for little hands.
text:
Great for a toddler's hands. A 7-inch Buzz Lightyear is perfect for little hands. I put the Buzz Lightyear toy next to a Sandra Boynton board book for size comparison.

When you squeeze his legs together, he says 1 of these phrases:
"To infinity and beyond!"
"Let's fly!"
"Now this is flying!"
"Rocket boosters engaged!"
"Engines are hot. Let's blast off!"
"Greetings, I am Buzz Lightyear. I am comin' in fast. Whoa whoa whoa whoa!"
"Here we go!"
"Thrusters to full power."
"Light speed, go!"
"Hyperdrive engine, ignite!"
"Full speed ahead."
"Hyperdrive, engaged."
"Launch into light speed, now!"
"Get ready to blast off."
"Lift off!"
"Flight path is clear, cadet. Get ready to blast off!"

When you press the red button on his chest, he says 1 of these phrases:
"Greetings, I am Buzz Lightyear. I come in peace."
"Whoa whoa whoa, hooyah!"
"Here we go!"
"Buzz Lightyear reporting for duty."
"Hooah"
"Follow me. I'll light the way."
"Whoa!"
"Three. Two. One. All systems activated."
"Yeah."
"Hiyah!"
"Ha ha ha ha ha ha."
"Hey now!"
"Heh heh heh heh, oh."
"Engaging full light sequence."
"Whoa whoa whoa whoa whoa!"
"Woo hoo!"
"Lift off lights, activate. Lift off lights, activated."
"To infinity and beyond."

Each of the phrases are often accompanied by a sound effect (e.g., rocket flight, rocket launch, beeping, laser shots, whooshing, etc.). Also, when you press the red button on his chest, sometimes you just hear sound effects (with no words).

Buzz's possible movements are simple, which is perfect for my 3-year-old. (The limited mobility of this toy may be less interesting for an older child.) This toy's main feature is that when you squeeze his legs together, his wings pop out, his right arm/fist raises up, and he speaks a phrase/makes a sound effect.

List of Buzz's possible movements:
- Can stand on his own.
- Cannot sit.
- Wings pop out when you squeeze his legs together.
- Right arm/fist raises into the air when you squeeze his legs together.
- Right arm/fist can move up and down (180 degrees).
- Right elbow does not bend.
- Right fist does not rotate at the wrist.
- Finger positions on either hand cannot be moved.
- Left elbow can bend (90 degrees).
- Left hand can rotate at the wrist (360 degrees).
- Left arm can rotate at the shoulder (360 degrees).
- Head cannot turn/rotate.
- Clear helmet does not open and close.
- Knees do not bend.
- Right leg can kick out to the side from standing position (< 90 degrees).
- Right leg can rotate at the hip (360 degrees).
- Left leg can kick out to the side from standing position (< 90 degrees).
- Left leg cannot rotate. (This leg is the one that engages the popping out of the wings and the lifting of the right arm/fist.)
- Ankles cannot bend.
- Cannot turn or bend at the waist.
- The only functional button are Buzz's suit is the big red one on his chest. The other buttons are decorative.
- The control panel in the forearm does not open.

title: Engaging toy, poorly composed songs, less educational than it could be.
text:
Overall, I think this tablet toy is good for kids that have limited screen time access. Two of the songs are the biggest "con" that caused me to write this review. The alphabet song stops after "z", not singing the "now I know my..." part. My daughter is used to singing the whole song, and constantly asks me why it's missing. Yes, we are in the "why" stage.
The color song presents the colors out of rainbow order in order to make the song flow. It is "lots of pretty colors/shining in a rainbow/red, orange, yellow/ purple, green and blue". It annoys me every.single.time. Either do a color song with a random order, or do a rainbow song in rainbow order. If a child's primary exposure to the colors of the rainbow is through this song, they will have to re-learn the rainbow colors in preschool.
My daughter also has a Leap Frog "laptop" that does many of the same things but better. Unlike this tablet, the Leap Frog includes phonetic sounds with the letters, which to me is very important for an alphabet toy. This tablet seems like the educational aspect was not fully thought through.

title: Great packs, great price
text:
So far I have to say, these packs are amazing. I’ve had them for 2 weeks already after flying my tired 1 year old CNHL packs. I could tell I difference immediately and it brought life back into my 700g freestyle setup. I’m using the 1500mah packs. The shape and build quality feels amazing (more squared than long) compared to my previous batteries. These packs are heat shrinked very tight and seem to have a strap of aluminum or G10 to protect the cells on the sides. I have crashed many times and these batteries are still in great shape. I will definitely be buying more and I high suggest these to anyone looking for new batteries.

Best part is, being on amazon, I get them the next day in most cases.

title: Adorable fall succulent building set!
text: I adore these little planted succulent garden building sets, and I was super excited to add one in fall colors to my collection! The pieces are normal size (similar to Legos), brightly colored, and they stick securely together without breaking apart. It was really straightforward and easy to assemble this set, and the instructions are clear and easy to follow. It only took my about an hour, if even, to assemble this one. There are a lot of unique shapes involved in these sets, which is always a plus. Another interesting thing is the variety of flower stamin they give you for the green tree-like plant - it comes with an assortment of pale lavender, see-through purple, and glittery clear colored stamin. The assembled product is simply lovely, and would surely make a good gift to lovers of the fall season and succulents in general. The price point makes it a great value for money. I cannot recommend enough, nor can I wait to purchase the other two variants in this series! 🥰🥰

title: The designs are super adorable and I love the variety offered in the ...
text:
I was so excited to get these for the upcoming Christmas season. The designs are super adorable and I love the variety offered in the set. I love that the ink is red and green as opposed to any other color. The size of them is great, perfect for kids or adults. As soon as I got them in the mail, I used them to stamp 2 of my Christmas cards. I laid those cards aside for a few hours as I went and did some stuff around the house. I came back to check on the stamps, and they were still wet and tacky. I thought okay, maybe they'll need to set overnight. The next morning I woke up and felt the ink on my Christmas card... still tacky and I managed to smear it on my card. So I took a piece of paper and stamped each stamp 4/5 times using different pressures, and let those set overnight. the next day NONE of them had dried! I ended up having to buy stickers to cover the smears on my Christmas cards. I am so disappointed in these!! I wouldn't recommend them to anyone with children, unless you want ink on everything.

The photos below show the stamps I had made 5 days later... let me repeat 5 DAYS LATER!!!

title: The hit of our lake trip!
text: THIS THING IS AMAZING! You 100000% have to have a pump to inflate it and it takes a little while but MAN is it worth it!!! We didn’t have a boat on our annual lake trip this year and I don’t love just swimming in the water in the cove. This was great for me who didn’t love feeling the fish touch me, for allowing more togetherness than several people in sep rafts floating all about, etc. The cooler and the shade sail made it so we pretty much just packed drinks, snacks, sunscreen, a speaker, etc in the morning and didn’t come back up to then house for most of the day! I loved that you could just lay in the mesh part under the shade and be completely in the water but not having feeling the fish. Was great for little ones too to be in the lake in a more secure way! Pro tip: get some rope or cord to tie up a few sides to the dock so you’re not worrying with this thing sailing right away. We left it blown up all week and many friends have purchased one after seeing ours! Made the week SO much more fun! We fit probably 5 adults plus some little ones easily! Best suited for 2-3 adults in each section (the laying out part and the shade part) at a time but is no problem with more.

title: Good gateway game to deeper boardgames
text:
Not a bad game but limited choices which actually allow you to control your game.
When you roll the dice, you are allowed to choose which dice you want to use for which purpose. This does sometimes lead to some agonizing decisions. However, to me, it usually just feels like you're choosing between two random things that still don't really allow you to control your fate.
The endgame is rather abrupt without a lot of tension. That really sums up a lot of the game. Oftentimes, things just happen. The players are along for the ride. It's not a deep game where every single decision you make is going to haunt you forever (whether or not that is a pro or con is up to you).
The game pieces are all very beautiful but the cardboard bits are great quality. You can definitely tell the priorities on the presentation. The box itself is unique and stands out in our game collection, even among hundreds of other games.
Final Verdict: Approved. For certain audiences. If you're looking for a deep hardcore Euro-style game, then look elsewhere. If you're looking for a game that introduces certain Euro elements but is approachable to beginning gamers then this might be a good choice.

title: Just like a real remote!
text:
I was debating whether to purchase this Vtech toy remote control over the Fisher-Price one and ultimately what swayed me was the color and look of this one--the remote controls we happen to have in our house, that my eight month old son loves to grab and play with at any chance, are all black, whereas the Fisher-Price remote is gray. I wanted one that was as similar as possible to our "real" remotes.

This play remote is really fun, with lots of buttons to press, and tons of different responses and songs. It even feels like a real remote when I pick it up and pretend to change channels just for fun sometimes before handing it to my son. I like that it has two different volume levels and fun colored flashing lights, and that the the buttons mimic actual real-life remote ones such as volume up and down control, up and down channel buttons, on and off buttons, number keys.

Sure, some of the phrases may seem like they're encouraging TV watching (as I've read from other reviews here before purchasing, and listening to it myself) but really, my eight month old baby is not going to end up a couch potato TV addict because of some sing-songy repetitions on a toy ;) --that will be solely based on my parenting choices, so I'm not too worried about that aspect!

I bought a Tickle Me Elmo for my daughter in the 90s and we still have it. He looks great for being that old. Sadly, this new Elmo does NOT measure up to his predecessor.

• His legs are not soft, as they are made with a spring type mechanism so he can kick.
• His body is not soft, as it is mostly a solid push button type mechanism.
• He does not always laugh when tickling his feet. This is very disappointing. Mostly, you must press his belly.
• I am afraid the push belly feature will stop working soon. I had another toy with the same feature that I had issues with. We'll see.
• He does giggle A LOT when pressing his belly, as long as you continue to push.
• He will kick his legs whether sitting up or laying down.
I am quite disappointed in this toy. It is not well made and I feel will not stand up to a toddler's play. Some things should not be "improved ". The original Tickle Me Elmo is definitely better than this one.

title: Quality Product
text:
I've always wanted to learn about electronics but was frustrated with the learn by reading process. This product is a wonderful teaching/learning device. It runs you through creating real working electronic devices. It also teaches you how to read electronic schematics. The breadboard can be a little frustrating until you get the hang of it.

I would be cautious of buying for a young child, but I think someone around 10 might be able to get into it without too much angst. As an adult (37 years), I find the instructions to be quite good and not juvenile like some other kits I came across.

Highly recommended if you're interesting in learning electronics for a hobby. You may find that you want to go further and get a degree in it.

title: Holds up to my 3 year old.
text: I still am completely shocked at how indestructible these dolls are, in comparison to some of the Disney frozen Dolls. While I have many of the more collectable versions of the Monster High dolls put up, I wanted to see how they would hold up to my 3 year old.  It is has been a fantastic experience for her, playing with these dolls.  They have super high quality hair that we put into a pony tail and maintain regularly.  Sure the arms come off, but that allows for quicker costume changes, which my little girl loves.  I keep a close eye on the parts and costume pieces, and overall I've enjoyed watching her creative play with these dolls. In contrast, my sister got her the Elsa and Anna dolls from Frozen and their hair went south within the first week, no matter what I've tried.  We lost the shoes immediately (since they slipped off right away - something that DOESN'T happen with the Monster High girls) and their clothing became tattered and worn within the first month.  Frankie, on the other hand, is still going strong, despite the DAILY household abuse she takes. I will totally be investing in the older line (I know nothing about the new versions) since I know they are a worthy investment.

title: Good plastic, floats, squirts, and hookable.
text:
Got this for the grand-kids to play with in the pool.

Pros:
* Nice plastic on all parts. Hard shiny kind on the pole, and tough squishy kind on the fish.
* Kids love the floaty fish, and being able to squirt is a bonus.
* We can have contests to see who can catch the most fish, fastest. (my kids are a bit older so gotta keep it interesting)
* Squirt guns are always a hit, no matter what shape they come in. (see cons)
* Pole is good to catch the fish, but short enough not to work well as a weapon. (see cons)

Cons:
* The younger kids may find it harder to squish the sturdy plastic. They require a lot of squishing to fill, and a firm squish to squirt, so while I can teach them to step on it, to fill, squirting is going to require them to build hand strength.

* The pole is hard plastic, so could be used as a weapon. It's pretty short, so only close combat, but still, watch the more aggressive kids, to be sure it's used for fishing, not hitting. It would definitely hurt, even with the rounded edges.

title: Works perfectly for us!
text:
This is a great bath toy storage container! Previously I had a mesh bag that was supposed to be durable and easy to clean....well, it ripped at the seam the first time my 20 month old grabbed it and he didn't pull hard, and then our water creates pink stains and the mesh bag would start to turn pink and I'd be cleaning it all the time. So it was clearly time for a better product. I bought this one based on other reviews, knowing that I did not want to permanently attach it to the wall (we rent) and thought I could at least repurpose the heavy duty suction cup hooks that came with the mesh bag. Well it worked perfectly - we have a glass surround around our bathtub so the suction cup hooks attach well to the glass and the 2 hooks side by side hold this organizer perfectly. It's not fallen down or moved by itself. It drains well and no water stains (yay!). We do have to play a bit of tetris to get all his toys and foam letters & numbers in, but that's only because we have too many of them! The only reason for four stars is for the method of attachment options; I only bought this because I knew I had the suction cup hooks...I would have been a little put off of buying extra hooks, but that being said - I don't know if there are other storage solutions that are better....so I think it is still probably the best option..?!
Update: I thought I'd list all the toys we can fit in here:
Foam alphabet letters and numbers 0-9
Stacking bath cups (stacked)
Plastic pull-string duck
Plui bath rain cloud (separated into 2 pieces)
And a couple of other small bath cups
Update: added some photos to help visualize.

title: generationxdad review Back to the future lego

Generation X throw back! Back to the Future!!! Hands down one of the best set of movies ever made. I'll never forget watching Dr. Emmett ‘Doc' Brown and Marty McFly traveling through time, riding a hover board, wild wild west, and the iconic DeLorean!!!! When I heard that Lego was going to create a DeLorean Lego I knew that my son and I were going to build this together! After watching all the movies it was time to sit down have have some enjoyable father and son time!

In my years I've spend a lot of time building Legos but nothing beats sitting down with my son and building Lego creations together!

After a little more then an hour we finished,

I love that with just a few changes you can change the DeLorean to match the individual movies. Well played Lego!!!!

title: Great Train Game
text:
Whistle Stop is a new introductory train game, that is just slightly above Ticket to Ride in terms of complexity. Many people will like this even more than Ticket to Ride as a gateway game. The game is a simple overall - place tiles, and choose to move your train forward along the line, collect cubes, and get special powers. We enjoyed the simplicity and elegance of gameplay, and how it bridges the very simple world of train games with the very complex 18XX style of games, as many of the scoring mechnics are similar (albeit much easier). The artwork on the majority of tiles is excellent, with the exception being the station tiles, which are largely black with words on them to tell what they do. We'll play this a lot at our house. 5 Stars.

title: Beautiful product that performs beautifully!  I would recommend.
text: When I received these beautiful rhythm scarves it was my idea to take them to a nursing home’s activities director to incorporate into one of the daily exercise activities, then donate the scarves to the program director to continue to use for that purpose.  Which is exactly what I did.  But what I did not know because I did not think to even ask, I was not allowed to film any of the seniors dancing with the scarves because of privacy laws.  I was not even permitted to take any pictures to post with my review.  I can tell you though there were 12 seniors that had a blast dancing with these scarves!  They swirled, twirled, whirled, and flounced about the room in motion with the dancers!  A sight to be seen by all.  And it is nice to know that once a week they will continue to have fun dancing to the oldies music and flying their colorful scarves all around the dance floor.  These scarves are the best product to put fun into people’s lives.  And from what I could tell from examining them they are made well.  The scarves are made from a silky, soft silk fabric.  The vibrant colors are a treat for all eyes, the scarves look like jewels set in motion when in use.  And the scarves also can be worn as an accessory to an outfit as well, set off with a piece of jewelry.  Each scarf has a finished rolled hem on all corners, and each are a perfect square 24” x 24”, and light weight so they dance and fly as you dance and jump and sail through the air with them.  The scarves would be perfect a fit for a pre-school class, or a kindergarten class, a dance class, or Zumba class, or just for at home for dress-up and day of fun and games.  I can think of a thousand uses for these scarves, including the Theatrical plays, and even comedy hour.  This product has so much potential it is unreal.  Great product!  I recommend these scarves to everyone.

title: Charge Your Batteries Every 3 Months.
text:
Charge your batteries every 3 months during off season/storage is strongly advisable. Beyond 6 months without charging, your risk of having bad (permanent) batteries increase significantly (oem or aftermarket). These batteries (oem or aftermarket) have monitoring circuitry builtin. They self discharge to about 50% (and stop there) if the batteries are not being used for about 1-2 week. The purpose is to prolong battery life.
HOWEVER, these circuitry continue to consume a very small amount of power and would eventually depleted the batteries if left unattended. Once these batteries drop below 9.6v, they are very likely become bad (permanently).

title: I've loved this car and played with it off and on ...
text:
I've got the bumblebee iteration of this car. The only difference is the body. I've loved this car and played with it off and on for years. I just upgraded to aluminum knuckles and have plans for additional upgrades if I can still find the parts. The issue is that Radio Shack discontinued the line several years ago, so it's hard to find parts for, though there is still a community that loves these guys. They're basically low cost nearly hobby grade RC's. All parts are accessible and replaceable. The stock plastic is prone to breaking if you aren't careful, but don't over-tighten screws and lugs and you'll be just fine.

The biggest shortcoming, in my opinion, is that the cars utilize AAA batteries. A rechargeable battery pack would go a long way toward improving the quality of the car and give more flexibility in how you run it. That being said, there are aftermarket options to upgrade, but it's expensive. You're best option is to find a good quality rechargeable AAA battery set and use that. There was a point where I was spending $20/week on batteries to play with this thing (oh, to be young, working full time, and have no bills again). It's a very fun car and a good entry into the hobby if you aren't sure you want to really get into it with a true hobby grade car.

title: Directions are unintelligible, the app is impossible.
text:
I went over the directions literally dozens of times doing my best to try and decipher what they actually were trying to say before I was able to get this thing to launch. I was finally able to get it in the air exactly two times.

As near as I can tell it isn't broken, but it doesn't seem to want to work now; the lights just blink, which if my deciphering is correct, means it's "correcting the frequency," whatever that means, which it apparently must do before it can take-off.

The first time I got it in the air (it was in the air for two seconds before it crashed, as I still have not been able to figure out how to control it) this "correcting the frequency" step only took a few seconds, and the second time it was still powered on from the first time so there was no need to do this step again. However, on the second flight (which lasted maybe ten seconds), when I pushed the button which, again as near as I could tell from the terribly written directions, was supposed to make it return to its take-off point, the thing just dropped out of the air like a rock and the battery popped out, so I had to go through the start-up process again. Now I don't know how long this "correcting the frequency" step is supposed to take, but I waited for quite a while, watching the lights blink in a seemingly mocking manner, before giving up on it. It is completely unresponsive at this point. All it will do is turn on and blink. I still have no idea how to actually make it do anything, and I have yet to figure out how to even connect it with the app on my phone in order to see the view through the camera.

Oh, and the diagram on the instructions clearly shows an entirely different model of drone, with completely different functions and features than the one that they came with, so the diagram itself it was also less than helpful. There is not even any description of how to turn the drone on; I had to figure out that the small marking that is molded into the plastic directly between the prop blades, which is very easy not to see, is actually a button if you press it hard enough and hold it for a moment.

Overall it was a very frustrating experience trying to get this thing to work, and I don't recommend it to anyone.

title: There's a reason why this has so many 5 star reviews!
text: If you haven't yet played this game or clicked the buy button, you're really in for a great treat (assuming you buy it, or play it).  As noted, this game has a really high number of five star reviews because the game is fun.  As many have noted, you get the benefits of a traditional role playing game in a sweet, short, fun card game that is enjoyable.  What's great in this game is that it can start out simple enough, but before you know it, you're doing everything you can to harm others and that's just part of the fun!  While the rules can get a little complicated at first, you quickly start to pick them put after playing a round or two, and you're enjoying yourself.  As some may have noted the game may get a little boring after a few dozen plays, but there is no shortage of expansions out there so you can add on to the game if you would like.  For the price and the fun you get from this game, you can't go wrong.  I play this with friends on our "game nights", and it's just a fun game to play in groups, and best of all if you're looking for something different from board games, you really get something that's different but also very fun.  I just wish I had learned about this sooner!

title: Game lovers, this is for you!
text:
We've had fun playing this DVD Family Feud Game as a family, it's much like the television version, a good variety of questions, including a thorough "how to play" selection to check out if your a first time user, just select that icon by using your own DVD remote, and within seconds, you're playing. The genre of questions remains the same as what you'd see on the television version of the game, some get a little "racey" like "What would you bring along on a first date?" One answer was "a condom..."

Negatives - Some answers I considered way off, like "what's a complaint people have with a valet service?" All the answers revolved around being too expensive, or the driver drove too fast, took too long. I thought of answers like, "he adjusted my seat, changed the radio presetting stations, moved the side mirrors, stole a CD..." So, some of the answers were unreasonable. Another question asked, "what's an appliance you might ask help moving," the number 1 answer was a sofa, but washer/dryer wasn't even listed. That didn't make sence to me. Also the speed round, I was dissappointed when the speed round came around and only the top rated answer to each question is revealed worth points. In the television version, more than one answer is valuated by points.

Positives - The on screen "how to play" icon will thoroughly walk you through the object of the game, it's simple and to the point. The game is fast paced, completely self explanatory, very compact, would be great to go on vacations with, takes no set up time, easy learning curve, the game prompts you what to do when. The bright and colorful display with attractive on screen game menus makes it fun to play with "elevator music" timing your responses.

Conclusion - It's a really fun game to play if you have at least 5 minutes to sit with your family and play a game. It's a go anywhere, creative, thought provoking game that everyone will enjoy contributing to.

title: returned it, hoping to try another one
text:
I was excited to buy this helicopter, as I wanted to get into RC flying and thought this would be a good beginner model, and having read all the other reviews many of which praise its stability, not just here on Amazon but other sites as well, so I ordered one. My first few times flying I was impressed with the sound of this thing and how well it lifted off the ground....but I soon discovered that despite all these claims of how easy to fly and how stable it is, mine seemed to always drift off from hover. I found myself often trying to re adjust the rotation trim knob. Well, I eventually chalked it up to "hey, its only a $30 copter and the electronics may not be that great."
But after my last flight, it fell to the floor (which is not unusual for a new flyer, and this copter does survive easily, most of the time) this one last time, the lower rotors now dont turn freely, and you can feel a binding in the gears. Under power...they will turn, but the copter just skitters along on the floor, since the lower rotors are not spinning at same speed as the uppers, So I am returning it. Not sure if I will get another of these micros, or something else.

title: One of the best dungeon crawler games I've played in a long time probably since Heroquest.
text:
It's already hit the table about 3 times in 1 week and the reviews are in. Keep it on the table.
It's one of the easiest, smoothest dungeon crawler games that I've played.
Character customization is nice, options are good.
Not many options in monsters to fight, but I changed out some of the miniatures from Conan to capture the true spirit of Sword and Sorcery.
(I personally like low fantasy in my S&S)
I like how the game handles death, shopping for gear is fun. Rulebook is thick but most of it is easy to understand. Do yourself a favor and download the double sided cheat sheet from BBG and you'll have a easier learning experience. Some of the youtube videos are too long and they screw up trying to teach it but if you're a visual learner it doesn't hurt to watch set up and the initial turn sequences.

title: LOVE THIS
text:
This is a fantastic set, especially for a kid who doesn't have a lot of Thomas toys yet. It's totally complete and you don't need to add anything to it to have hours of fun playing. Although it is even more fun if you can add another set and/or some engines and cars. We have the Cranky dock set, which comes with a magnetic crane and cargo, and we have Harvey the engine with a magnetic crane arm, and both are perfect for this set. We load up the trains with farm cargo, haul it to the ocean and load it on the boat, then he takes it away. It's perfect.

The set is extremely well made and has lots of fun little touches that kids love, like the little window in the barn that the chickens or dog can look through, the fun cargo you can load up, and the beautiful paint job on the engine.

There is a lot of track and there are a bunch of ways you can set it up. The pictures are confusing and it's easy to run out of pieces if you design your own track, so if your kiddos are little you might find yourself having to set it up for them each time. A couple of the parts (like the ramps) only work if they're in the right spot which is hard for a lot of kids.

This set is expensive but it's a fantastic value in terms of Thomas toys. You get a ton of stuff and it only costs a little more than other sets that have only a few things in them. I also think it's great that it's a standalone set that doesn't require a lot of other stuff.

title: Not a good purchase
text:
National Geographic does not make this product or even support it at all (great company?). Its made by a third party and just brand licensed. There are no spare parts available for purchase. The drone is definitely NOT durable (see other comments).
Regarding parts National Geographic advised me to contact the actual manufacturer which is listed on the box, I contacted them only to be told they do sell replacement parts. This is a very fragile drone and I had a blade break just landing on grass. If a blade breaks and you take off again its not under control at all and can be easily lost.
The return to home feature does not work that well and the flips are very exaggerated. I wish i spent more money on a better drone.
If anyone knows of any 3rd party parts to replace blades and guards I love love to hear. I've tried a couple that i thought might fit, one set of guards fitted but fell out during flight and damaged a blade. I would have been better off spending a few extra bucks on a better more durable drone than this one. Also note that although it comes with a set of 4 replacement blades you can not replace the same blade 4 times, they are in rotating and counter rotating pairs so you only have two replacements for any blade.

title: Convenient, portable Chess Set for people on the go
text:
Overall, I like this chess set. It is a great value for the price, and fulfills it's purpose, to play chess on travel or on the go. For example, my son and I played chess at a theme park while waiting in line for rides, and my son uses it on the school bus.

Positives: Case is well-built, seems strong enough, my son threw the closed set to me 15 feet away, landing it on the pavement, and the case was not damaged. Pieces really stick to the board, and are short enough you can close the box, put it in your backback, get it out later, and your game is intact. It's big enough to see and move the pieces (I've had tiny sets). But it's small enough to fit in a backback and to hold easily with one hand while moving pieces with the other. Case is attractive.

Negatives: Case and pieces are plastic, and on the aforementioned throw, one of tiny tabs marking a rook broke off. All the pieces are the same size, and the bishops look too much like pawns -- but people have fixed that by putting a dot of paint on the Bishop heads, and we will do that soon.

Biggest negative: The paint is wearing off the black squares, and we've only had this a month or two. The problem is the magnets are strong, and if you slide your pieces, the friction is like sanding the board. You really need to pick up the pieces to move them, but then you have to be careful because if you go too close you can magnetically pull other pieces off the board. I don't know if this is peculiar to our board, because it seems a thin coat of clear finish would have solved this problem. We might contact the company to see if we can get a replacement, but it looks like it would be easy enough to repaint if we had to.

But the paint doesn't come off MUCH, so it's still easy to tell which square is which.

title: Blow up Dolphin scares pond predators
text: I was using a similar product (penguin) and had to settle for the dolphin as the penguin was no longer available at this cheap price.  These are pretty cheap, last for sometimes 2 to 3 seasons floating around on my koi pond. I had bought many other shapes to float on my pond to keep the Heron and Osprey away.  I leave them on the pond all year long. These have done the trick for me for about 8 years.  Some don't inflate right out of the box, some only last maybe six months, diaphram can rupture between the air and water weight in the bottom but I don't mind. Of course if there is no breeze, they don't move. By filling the bottom chamber with water, high winds don't displace them outside of the pond. Might not be the prettiest pond addition but watching a prize fish in the talons of an eagle or little birds killing themselves in a netting cover trying to bathe was not for me!  They are easily removed if you are entertaining and don't want to look silly. I'm sticking with the bobbing dolphins!

title: Hour 1, but still 4 star
text:
So this came to our house 3 days ago. I got it put together after the family headed off to bed, so being a dad I decided that it needed to be tested to insure that it would work. I began by pressing all the button on the inside. Honestly, it is really cool. The little “radio” is fantastic and I imagine that my boy will love it. The lights can be toggled on or off and the push button power button is awesome (I wish my truck had that). Grabbing the parental remote, I paired it and then began moving forward and back. Ok, it works well, has a soft take off and stop. I then attempted to turn the wheels. I heard a cracking sound, was a bit perplexed and lifted the front of the truck up. Turns out that the plastic gear that connects the steering column shaft to the RC motor for parent control busted and half of it fell out. My little guy could still drive it if I let him, but since a huge reason I purchased it was for the parental control (he’s 3) I won’t let him yet.

Aside from that, everything seems to work well and is fairly high quality. This thing has actual suspension and huge tires. I am going to see if I can get a replacement gear, and from everything I’ve read so far, the company seems to be fairly responsive and easy to work with. I will update this when I get things working to let you all know how it goes. But overall, I would give this thing a solid 4 star just for design and construction (minus the gear).

Update: If the control gear for the steering breaks, a 3/4" CPVC coupling fits perfectly over the middle and is more durable (need to cut a notch out).

So we turned this into the batmobile for halloween. It lasted a full 2 hours of driving before it died right as we got back home. My boy loves this thing and loves having dad drive him around (I"m on my wife's account). Obviously since we've only had it 2 ish weeks, I can't speak about longevity, but as I said before, the quality seems good and it works well. Well worth the price (pretty inexpensive). If you're thinking about it, get it.

Update 01-2023
Yes it still works and yes I would still recommend this rider.
I've had to replace the battery, but that is it.

title: This dragon is HUGE
text:
I'd previously seen this dragon in person, but I still can't get over just how BIG it is. And let me tell you, my players have been extra nervous since it arrived (they know my propensity for throwing dragons at them). It's a great model to keep on the shelf overlooking the gaming table, a real eye catcher. I look forward to the day they are high enough level I can take it down and have them face it.

MINOR drawbacks:
- The clamshell it arrived in (inside the box) is VERY fragile and arrived broken; however the mini itself was unharmed and now lives on a shelf outside the box.
- the talons at the trailing side of the wings are really sharp. I've stabbed myself a couple times handling the model. They really didn't need to be nearly that sharp. I've heard they're also fragile, so I've been extra careful around handling them since mine have not broken.
- The mounted drow rider takes away from the model. I know he's there for a specific purpose, but it's already very specific to have a fight with such a giant white dragon. It didn't need to rider. Thankfully he's not molded in, so he can be removed when I finally do get to field this dragon.

title: Fun with potential as a passive aggressive revenge gift
text:
Initially I was thrilled about how challenging the picture was, as many shaded areas looked like they could go together, and they're nearly identical pieces. I found the letter grid on the back useful for sorting out the puzzle and great for breaking it into sessions or splitting up the work when someone else wanted to play.

However, there were four pieces that had lost their backing that I needed to glue together, one of which I accidentally put on backwards, oops! (I recommend reserving fixing pieces until you're almost done with the puzzle. I was thinking it would be good to give the glue time to dry, but taking a break for glue drying and getting it right would have been the best route.)

Also, this was probably one of the most difficult puzzle break-aparts I've ever experienced. It took me probably about 20 minutes to get the pieces all apart at the end. It was nice for being able to check the letter grid, but just about every piece was a fight when it came to separating. They would get stuck even if they weren't the right piece and you (sometimes accidentally) bumped the bits together (rowr.)

All of that said, my youngest was overjoyed with the sweetness of the scene and was delighted to get the poster when we finished the puzzle. As I wiped the sweat from my brow after putting the puzzle away, their smile made it all worth it.

Initially I thought I wouldn't want to give this to someone with my name attached, but then I thought about some of the nightmare puzzles people have casually given us over the years, and this one was more fun than most of those. If you're feeling nice, you could re-gift this to someone you know would want to use it as a picture, and when they're done they could probably pick it up and stand it against the wall, no need for glue.*

* This statement is in no way backed by the distributor of the product.

title: Got this for my cats
text:
I got this for my cats to play with. Very soft and surprisingly light.

The page says it's 1.1 lb, which seems about right. I have the "Medium" 19 inch model. It's 19 inches from the tip of the nose to the base of the tail--the same size as my cats. The tail is another 17 inches.

In terms of safety, the included tags say it's not recommended for children under 12 months because of shedding fabric. They don't mention small parts. The eyes are the only small parts I see. They are somewhat recessed and don't seem like they would fall out easily, but I suppose you wouldn't want to give this to infants anyway. The "plastic pellets" are mainly inside Sacha's paws and abdomen. For cat toys, what you generally want to look out for is loose threads, because cats like to eat string. Sacha doesn't have any loose threads at the moment.

Jury's still out on whether my cats will play with it. They sometimes need a few days to adjust to new things.

Hand-washing only according to the manufacturer.

Made in Indonesia.

title: Very good toy
text:
This is a really good toy, my daughter absolutely loves it and I was even impressed with it. It's definitely worth the $30 it's usually priced at.

It has a lot of features. A slide, hammock, elevator, the little raceway and merry-go-round. I think the cutest feature is the swing at the top. You twist it up and when you set a magnetized pet on the top it begins to spin by itself. No batteries needed, very cool.

But it does come apart very easily, as do most littlest pet shop toys. It's best to pick it up by the base when you move it. Even though it doesn't weigh much if you pick it up by the towers they will come off. It is very simple to put them back on though, it only takes about 2 seconds. It's not a big issue but it does happen.

It does only come with two pets though, so if you don't already have extra littlest pets you may want to buy some more to go with this.

I would recommend this for any child. I know it's targeted towards girls but my nephew sat and played with it for over an hour the other day. It keeps kids busy and happy for hours on end.

title: It's not a $500.00 drone, but does the Job as a Trainer and Fun.
text:
Obviously, this is not a 'professional' drone, so I would not expect 'professional' quality pictures or video.
For the price of the drone, the drone does the job as a trainer and fun.
Range of the drone can vary according to terrain.
Some reviews I read indicated they had a fixed camera on the drone they received.
The drone I was sent, the camera can be swiveled up and down manually.
Had to play with it to get the correct view angle I wanted.
I don't know if this is an improvement on the earlier E58 models.
The drone seems to zip along pretty good. Maneuverability is good.
Easy to control for a drone without GPS.
I found the secret to this drone is, trim the drone immediately after it takes off.
After trimming, the drone is very stable.
As far as wind, I flew it a couple of times in very a light breeze and seemed to do ok.
I would not fly this drone in anything other than a very soft breeze.
It's light and without GPS will not do well in the wind.
Other than that, it flies quit well for a mid $30.00 drone.
Only negative is the batteries last about 7 minutes a piece.
The positive is that this drone has a very large parts selection from props, to batteries here and on the internet..
I ordered some 1200ma batteries to extend flight time.
In all, don't expect the features of an expensive drone.
I do a lot of camping and hiking.
Personally, I would take a cheap drone like this hiking or camping.
If I lost this, no big deal. If I lost a $500 drone, that could hurt the pocket book.
The E58 overall does a good job for a drone at this price point for a training drone, backpacking/camping drone.
Or just the fun factor.
I bought another one for my wife.
Easy to get parts for..

title: Does everything.
text:
When you were a kid, you probably wondered why your toys didn't do everything. Why didn't Hot Wheels cars have opening doors, trunk space, and a three-year warranty? Why didn't your action figures talk and have individually articulated fingers?

The Alternators line said, "Why indeed," and proceeded to make Transformers that did everything. A convertible top? Check. Opening doors, hood, trunk? Check. Chromed wheels? Stickshift and parking brake? Front wheels with a steering linkage? You get the idea. Not even the Masterpiece transformers do as much, individually, as the Alternators, though some come close.

And then, when you tried to transform one, you learned why toys didn't do everything. Transforming one is "fun" in the same way that playing Dwarf Fortress is fun: you either manage to wrest fun from the iron grip of frustration, or you take a mangled transformer back to the store and spend the $20 crying into your beer instead. Windcharger/Decepticharge is no exception.

What separates this toy from its fellow Alternators is how well it uses all those opening doors and adjustable seats to make a robot. The seats fold inside the chest. The doors fold cleanly onto the shins. The rear spoiler and trunk even become part of the chest piece. In short, this guy does everything the Movie transformers did well years ahead of his time, and he's even Bumblebee yellow.

This is not a transformer you buy because you're attached to the character (seriously, "Decepticharge" sounds like the name of a rather suspect credit card company). This is a transformer you buy because it's a miracle of engineering.

title: I Won a Game!!
text: I love Uno.  I like Blokus, but I have never won a game of any other version of the game (original, Trigon, 3D) because my husband is a master at the visual planning required.  The first game of Blokus Shuffle was very fun and he won.  The second time we played, I won.  Our 9 year old and 12 year old sons enjoy it, too.  At first one was reluctant to play because he isn't an Uno fan.  He enjoyed the first game and was resilient enough to complete the second game.  This is one good skill that games like this can teach.  As one of the cards allows you to warp (relocate) another players piece while another let's you play like you are a different color (wild).  Both of these actions can be upsetting when you have planned out your moves.  It's all part of the fun and unpredictability that I love about this version.  The kids just need to be reminded that it's not a personal attack and it's all part of the game.  That is a great lesson for out boys.  As with all versions of Blokus, I would recommend being cautious with the pieces so that younger kids and cats (or other pets) don't run off with the pieces as these are unique and not easily replaceable.

text: Probably my favorite game because it's easy to teach, fun to play, and hard to master.  This is great for all ages.  It really evokes an visceral response; it can get intense and competitive (depending on the players) and almost everyone I show it to loves it.  Start with the base rules: pick up the object matched on the card or the one not represented by shape or color before anyone else.  When you want more try the rule: if there's a book on the card, say the answer instead of picking it up.  If you get it first, you get a card as a point, and the person with the most points at the end wins.  This also mixes well with Ghost Blitz 2 expanding to 10 objects and twice as many cards that you can put together for a more challenging game.  Plus you can add house rules like if there's a ghost, pick up the object that's the color of the ghost.

title: An Analysis Size Silicone Board!!
text:
First, I am a tournament chess player (1700) and I was looking for a silicone analysis board. These are boards where the chess squares are 1.75" to 1.88" instead of the standard 2.25". It does not sound like much of a difference, but for smaller chess sets it makes a huge difference. I found what I was looking for here - I would probably give it 4.5 stars instead of 5, but am rounding up because the sellers very willingly sold me a board only and not the silicone set.

Pros
- It is silicone and will fold up and then lay flat as a pancake
- It is in an analysis size, the squares on the board are roughly 1.88 inches
- It was reasonably priced, I bought mine for $20 including shipping. That is a little more that your typical silicone board, but this is the only one in an analysis size.
- I don't know if this is a pro/con, the material is actually a little thicker than most silicone boards. I would have preferred thinner material so that it was more compact-able.

Cons
- The color of the squares are light green. My preference is for dark green, your mileage may very.

Bottom Line
This is the board that I stuff into my drawstring bag with my House of Staunton Reykjavik set. My analysis size vinyl boards are now in the back of the closet. If you need an analysis size silicone board, this is the only one I could find on the internet and will be the one I have in my backpack.

Photos
The first photo is with my HoS Reykjavik set on the XSKN board. For comparison, I put a vinyl board, analysis size, in the background. You can see how the vinyl squares are a darker green. Also, the XKSN board comes with a Starbucks logo in the corner....

The second photo shows that I was able to get the board in the bag with my set. I left it in the bag for a couple of days -- still came out flat as a pancake.

title: You get what you paid for….keep your expectations low, ain’t no Lego
text:
[[VIDEOID:7eae1045f8833c46021e2a6408c37bb1]] I like to give some background on me so there is some context to why I point out the things I do in my reviews. I have a degree in Model Building and I’ve been in the industry for over 23 years with all of it being focused on consumer products. While my degree isn’t specific to putting Lego’s or plastic model car kits together like most people think, it does revolve around designing and building prototypes with a high level of attention to details and precision, which is a must in my industry. So my review of this kit isn’t purely from the standpoint of a 35+ year fan of Lego’s, but also from a “this is what I do for a living” standpoint.

Onto the review. If you’re looking for the elevator pitch on this kit, it would be to save your money for a Lego brand kit. While the price tag on Funwhole kits is enticing, it’s a classic you get what you paid for scenario.

First off the, the product packaging was really nice. Nice box, good color on the graphics, nice bags for the parts and no dead space in the box like many of the Lego kits. The manual was also of very good quality, pretty good coloring on the pages, although some of the colors made it tough to distinguish between bricks of similar colors and/or if it was say a dark brown color it was sometimes hard to see if there were studs on top of the plate or if it was a smooth top plate. The manual did have notations tell you if a part was a 1x6 plate or a 1x8 plate so that was a nice add. I’ve already forgotten if there were 1:1 scaled photos to ensure proper brick sizing, but I feel like there was not with the Funwhole kit (sorry, I’ve been doing a lot of kits lately!).

The first thing I noticed when starting the assembly was how quickly things started to warp. Plates would start out nice and flat but as soon as I started snapping plates together things started getting wonky. Not much of an issue with the bricks, but more so the flat plate pieces. Overall though the bricks snap together securely, although they do take a little more effort to push together tightly than say an authentic Lego brick. One thing that became apparent during the build is that I don’t think anyone at Funwhole has ever put together a Lego kit. Their building technique is extremely weak. When building walls they do a poor job of interconnecting pieces, staggering pieces for a stronger stack, etc. Very week building overall. Also, they have a lot of instances where they have a multi stud brick or plate only connected to the previous layer by a single stud. This causes poor alignment, a weak structure and nothing feels nice and straight. The last big area of concern for me with this kit was the roof and dormers. The roof is built for a 90 degree gable end, but the gable of the house is less than that. So the roof teeter totters when you set it on the house. This in turn cause more issues when you try to install the dormers as they keep wanting to pop. The lighting element for each dormer only adds to this problem even more and is the frustration I tried to show in my video clip.

Overall, I don’t think I ever had the thought of not wanting to finish a building kit like I did with this one. It was frustration the entire time and it didn’t bring me the joy, happiness, satisfaction, etc. that I look for when doing this hobby. Of course the gold standard is Lego, but man, if your going to make a product to compete with them make an effort with a higher quality product. They’re so close, just a few tweaks and you could give them a run for the money!

title: Little minds are hungry-feed them with this learning puzzle!
text:
Kids like puzzles,so why not get them started early and teach them at the same time! I gave this to my 3 year old nephew. My husband said it was wasted money, he was too young. Well, he has since changed his tune. The little boy was intrigued by all the different shapes and bright colors. There is also painted pictures on each state depicting something that relates to the state. Under each state is the name of the capitol city.
My nephew loved this immediately. He studies the pictures, asks the name of the states, and has fun putting the united states back together. He now knows where he lives, where I live, and where various other family members live, When they went on vacay this January, he grabbed his puzzle to see where they were going. He actually grasped the fact that they were going to travel through 3 other states before they got to their Florida house. Hellooo? I know many adults who probably don't know THAT! He is having fun, and has no idea that he is learning so much, When he starts school, he will be ahead of his class, at least in this department. I am very satisfied with the product and the impact this puzzle has made on my nephew. It has proven to be much more than I ever hoped it would be, and it was well worth the money. In today's world, we need to seize every opportunity to share knowledge with the young minds in our family. And we need to catch them before the internet or social media hijacks their little minds! This is truly a learning tool that is fun, who could ask for more?

title: Soft yet interactive toy perfect for those looking for a 12 month + toy
text: When I saw this puppy I knew that it would be pefect for my daughter for her 1st birthday.  As soon as she opened it she was so excited and began dancing to the music.  After getting "Violet" out of the box I was able to easily connect her to our laptop and within minutes began customizing her for my daughter.  You are able to chose from three categories as well as a way to add your child's name to your leapfrog pup.  The software that you use offers multiple pronunciations of each name and you chose which is correct for your child.  After that you are shown a large list of foods and you can select one that is your little one's current favorite, next you can pick their favorite animal from yet another large selection and then finally you pick their favorite color.  All of those things were simple and easy to change so when my daughter's tastes change it will only take a few minutes to update her pup.  After adding in all of the favorites you are shown a list of songs that you can "select" or "deselect" to play during your child;s sleepy time music.  Since I did not see any that were huge for my 1 yr old I randomly selected a few.  The last step was then selecting playtime music, since my daughters birthday wa right around Christmas there were some Christmas songs available so I am guessing they add new ones every so often.  I again chose a few of the more popular songs and then added one that sang and spelled her name.  Once I was done I set all of the information to the dog and unplugged the usb and closed the back of the toy.  From the very first song this toy was a huge hit with my children, even the 2 and 4 yr old want to help their little sister play with it.  Buying toys for a 1yr old can be hard since they are at an age where they learn and grow so quickly, this seemed to bridge that gap buy having a toy that she can dance and babble at but I can personalize and help her learn along the way.  I would buy this again in a heartbeat and may be purchasing two more if everyone is still begging for their own later down the road.

title: Great product for a great price
text:
Great game if you know how to play. If you dont know how to play...google it as there are no instructions here but honestly its simple.

Every gets 3 (currency, dollars work great)
Roll 1 dice for every currency you have
Note what face comes up (circle = keep one, star = put one in the middle, left/right = give one in that direction) take those actions.
Play until one person is left with at least one currency in front of them, they roll and take action on face.
If they roll and are still the last with currency they get everything in the pot.

Note: If all currency goes to the pot, everyone stars fresh with 3 currency (keeping the pot as it is) and play game again. Great way to double down.
